about.title: About
about.p1: ravazque.info shows statistics for 42 Madrid Fundación Telefónica students, built on the 42 API. It is an independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by 42. Sign in with your 42 account and it reads your own data from the 42 API: logged-in time and seats, projects and attempts, evaluations received and given, feedback, correction points, skills and events.
about.p2: It is only for students whose main campus is 42 Madrid Fundación Telefónica and who have started the 42cursus: students, transcenders and alumni. Staff, pisciners and blackholed or frozen accounts cannot use it.
about.p3: The 42 API limits how many requests an application can make, so your data can be refreshed once an hour. The first load takes about a minute.
about.p4: Some figures are inferences and the page says so: where you sat during an evaluation comes from your login sessions, and the XP of each project is a calculation.

policy.who.list: Students, transcenders and alumni whose primary campus is 42 Madrid Fundación Telefónica.
Signing in requires your 42 account and accepting this policy.
Staff, pisciners, and blackholed or frozen accounts have no access; access is checked again at every refresh.
policy.purpose.title: Purpose
policy.purpose.body: To show you your own 42 history: logged time and seats, projects and attempts, exams, pace, evaluations given and received, the people you crossed paths with, your promo and the coalitions.
Data is never sold, never used for advertising or profiling, no decisions about you are made with it, and there are no usage analytics.
policy.from_api.title: Data obtained from the 42 API
policy.from_api.list: About you: login, name, photo, campus and coalition; cursus, level, skills, projects, marks, exams, Common Core and blackhole dates, achievements, titles and quests; login sessions and the computers you used; events; evaluations given and received with their dates, marks, flags, comments and your own feedback; correction points and wallet. The intra's own daily logtime, the 42 groups on your profile, and the points you have given your coalition (amount, kind and date).

About other students: their login, name and group (their milestone, OuterCore, alumni, blackholed, pisciner or staff), as they appear in your own evaluations and teams, and, for your evaluations of the last 60 days only, the computer the other side (your corrector, or the students you evaluated) was logged in at during that evaluation and, for the students you evaluated, how many minutes after its start they logged in when they were late. It is worked out from their login sessions of that day, which are read and dropped at once: only the seat and those minutes are kept, inside your report. For your 30 closest contacts, how many times each one evaluated the others (Your circle): it is read from the evaluations they gave and only those counts are kept, inside your report. Their photos are never loaded. Promo and coalition figures are counts without names. For your place in Madrid, every hour in which someone opens a page the server reads from the 42 API the level of every Madrid 42cursus student and keeps only the levels of those in the Common Core or OuterCore, frozen and alumni, in memory: no login, name or id.
Only data the intra already shows to members of the 42 Network is used.
policy.generated.title: Data generated by the site
policy.generated.list: Session: a random id in the __Host-session cookie; in the server's memory, your login, name, photo link, coalition colour and a request token.
Your analysed report: the original is kept in your browser (IndexedDB). The server keeps a signed copy in memory to draw your pages, for one hour after its last use; it is never written to disk.
Record of your acceptance of this policy: a keyed hash of your 42 id, the accepted version and the date. It is the only thing the server writes to disk.
Hourly refresh limit: a keyed hash of your 42 id, in memory, for at most 60 minutes.
Sign-in attempts: a keyed hash of your IP address, in memory, for 10 minutes, to prevent sign-in abuse.
Your photo: in memory for an hour, so that the image CDN is not asked for it again.
After "Delete my data": a keyed hash of your 42 id and the date, in memory for 30 days, so that an older copy of your report is refused.
Operations page, for the site's owner only: counters (requests, extractions, memory) and who is signed in right now (login, name, when). It is in memory and goes with the server's restart.
policy.basis.title: Legal basis
policy.basis.list: Consent (Art. 6.1.a GDPR) for your own data and the data the site generates: you give it by ticking the box and signing in, and it is recorded.

Legitimate interest (Art. 6.1.f GDPR) for showing the login, name and group of the students in your own evaluations and teams, and where the other side of your recent evaluations sat, which the intra already shows to the 42 Network. They can object at any time (see Exclusion).
policy.terms.title: Terms of use
policy.terms.list: The data comes from the 42 Network and must stay within it: do not share, publish or redistribute other students' data.
Bulk extraction, automated access and attempts to bypass access controls or limits are forbidden.
Your session is personal: do not share it.
Misuse may lead to loss of access.
The service is provided as is. Data can be up to an hour behind: the intra is always the official source.
policy.liability.title: Disclaimer and limitation of liability
policy.liability.body: The site is a free, personal and independent project, provided "as is" and "as available", with no warranty of any kind, express or implied, including fitness for a particular purpose, accuracy or availability. It may be unavailable, change or stop at any time, and its figures may be incomplete, delayed, estimated or wrong; the 42 intranet is always the authoritative source.

To the fullest extent permitted by law, {controller} shall not be liable for any direct, indirect, incidental or consequential loss or damage arising from the use of, or inability to use, the site, or from reliance on anything it shows. Nothing in this policy excludes or limits liability that cannot lawfully be excluded, such as for intent or gross negligence, nor affects your mandatory rights under data-protection or consumer law.

You are solely responsible for how you use the data shown and for complying with 42's own terms. Access and the service may be restricted, suspended or withdrawn at any time, in particular in case of misuse.

"42", "42 Network" and related names and logos belong to their respective owners; this project is not affiliated with, authorised or endorsed by them and claims no rights over them. The site's own source code is released under the AGPL-3.0 licence.
policy.retention.title: Retention
policy.retention.list: Session: 7 days, renewed while you use it; it also ends when the server restarts.
Report: in your browser until you sign out or delete your data; the server's copy, one hour after its last use or at once with "Delete my data".
Acceptance record: 2 years after your last sign-in.
Refresh limit: 60 minutes. Sign-in attempts: 10 minutes. Photo: one hour. The mark after "Delete my data": 30 days.
Language, theme, accent, starred sections, widgets and which pages you have already opened: in your browser until you clear them or use "Delete my data".
policy.security.title: Security
policy.security.list: Encrypted connection only (HTTPS with HSTS) and a strict content security policy.
Your 42 access token is used once to identify you and never stored; tokens never reach the browser.
HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite session cookie; every action that changes something carries a request token.
No database: the server keeps sessions and report copies in memory only. A report your browser hands back is accepted only with the server's own signature for your account.
No third-party cookies, trackers or scripts.
In case of a security breach, the people affected and, where required, the authority will be notified.
policy.third.title: Third parties
policy.third.body: Data is never sold or shared for any other purpose. The site is reached through Cloudflare (Cloudflare, Inc.), which carries the connection between your browser and the server. The HTTPS encryption ends on its network, so your IP address and what you request and receive pass through it decrypted before being encrypted again towards the server, possibly outside the EU, under its own privacy policy (cloudflare.com/privacypolicy). Transfers to the United States rely on its certification under the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework; transfers to other countries, or if that certification lapses, on the EU Standard Contractual Clauses of its Data Processing Addendum (cloudflare.com/cloudflare-customer-dpa). The server runs on Amazon Web Services (AWS) in the EU (Stockholm): the server's copy of your report stays in that machine's memory and the record of your acceptance on its disk, under AWS's privacy notice (aws.amazon.com/privacy). The server only talks to the 42 API (api.intra.42.fr) and its image CDN (cdn.intra.42.fr); your browser contacts no other service through this site unless you follow a link out: a login in a table or list opens that student's page on acerezo.top, another independent site, in a new tab; that site then receives the login you chose and your IP address, under its own terms, and is not told which page you came from.
policy.rights.title: Your rights
policy.rights.list: Access: see which of your data is stored (all of it is on your dashboard and in your browser).
Rectification: data comes from the intra, so it is corrected there.
Erasure: "Delete my data" removes the server's copy and clears this site's storage in your browser; signing out removes the report from your browser. To delete the source data, contact 42.
Restriction of and objection to processing, and portability of your data.
Withdraw your consent at any time by deleting your data and signing out; this does not affect earlier processing.
policy.rights.body: Requests are answered within one month. You can also lodge a complaint with the Spanish data protection authority (AEPD, www.aepd.es).
policy.exclusion.title: Exclusion
policy.exclusion.body: If you appear in someone else's report and want to be excluded, write to {email} with your login: you will be shown as "Hidden" in every report, with a number that only tells people apart within that report and no name, photo or seat, and your login goes from team names and comments too. The evaluations you took part in still count in the other person's figures: only who you are goes. A comment where someone wrote your real name can't be caught automatically: tell us if you find one.

policy.cookies.list: IndexedDB: your report, with the server's signature.

localStorage: language, theme and accent colour; the sections you star, and your Profile widgets, under your login; that you have seen the star's tip; the date of your saved report; and which pages you have already opened, so their charts draw in only the first time or when you reload.

profile.title: Profile
landing.f_time: Every hour you logged, per day, week and month, and a calendar of the days you came. Your longest sessions, streaks and the time of day you work. The exact computers you used most, on the cluster plan, with your first and last time at each, and the 50h / 80h logtime bonus with when the next one arrives.
landing.f_evals: Every evaluation you gave and received: when it was, how long it lasted and how far ahead it was booked. The seat you were at and the seat of who evaluated you, on the cluster plan. Marks, Outstanding and other flags, the ratings both ways with their comments, and the hours you gave the community.
landing.f_projects: Every attempt of every project on one timeline: team, mark, moulinette results, who corrected it and when. Your retries and the days each project took to validate, every exam try, and your XP per project and by technical domain, with a portfolio you can download.
landing.f_people: The correctors you met most and the Outstanding flags they gave you, and everyone you crossed paths with, searchable by login, project or seat. Your circle of students who evaluate each other, connections grouped by where they are today, and your teammates with the projects you shared.
landing.f_coalition: The points you gave your coalition, by source and by month, and the latest ones with the project or evaluation behind each. The standings of the Madrid coalitions and your place in your promo by level.
landing.f_profile: Level and its curve, XP per month and skills for the 42cursus and the piscine. Wallet, correction points, achievements, events and quests, and your blackhole or, in the OuterCore, an estimate of when you become alumni.
about.why: Mainly to learn: to work with the 42 API from end to end, and to give 42 Madrid Fundación Telefónica students what the intra keeps scattered or does not show at all. How many hours you have really spent on campus and where you sat, whom you evaluated and who evaluated you, how long each evaluation took, how your projects and retries add up over time. All of it about you, in one place.
about.feature_1: Logged time per period, per day and per month, a calendar of every day on campus and your longest sessions
about.feature_2: The cluster plan with the computers you used most, and every login session
about.feature_3: Evaluations given and received over time, with marks, flags, duration and how far ahead they were booked
about.feature_4: Where you and your corrector were sitting during each evaluation (inferred from login sessions)
about.feature_5: Who evaluated you, whom you evaluated, ratings both ways and the feedback you received
about.feature_6: Every project and attempt on one timeline, with retries, marks, moulinette results and correctors
about.feature_7: Exams with every try, and the days each project took to validate
about.feature_8: XP by technical domain (the intra's RNCP tags) and a portfolio export as CSV
about.feature_9: Your circle of students who evaluate each other, connections by rank, and your teammates
about.feature_10: Coalition points by source, your latest contributions and why, and the 50h / 80h logtime bonus with a forecast
about.feature_11: Your place in your promo by level, and the standings of the Madrid coalitions
about.feature_12: Level, pace, skills, wallet, correction points, your blackhole or, in the OuterCore, an estimate of when you become alumni
about.feature_13: Light and dark mode, English and Spanish, in the 42 colour or your coalition's
about.pages: A Vue and TypeScript app served by the same server; the charts are drawn in your browser as SVG and HTML, with no chart library.
about.backend: Go (standard library only), sign-in with 42 OAuth2, and batched, paginated requests to the 42 API.
about.infra: Docker Compose and Caddy (reverse proxy and TLS). No database: the server keeps your report in memory for an hour, and the original lives in your browser.
about.beta: This project is in beta and changes often. If you find a bug or have an idea, open an issue or write to ravazque on Slack.
